subject: Escalation: Nimble pilot — ramp schedule & early-term opt-out
message_1_subject: Proposal: Pilot + ramp schedule — Nimble Health
message_1_body:
Hi Hannah / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile for their conversational triage use case. Procurement asked me to share a few requests we'd like reflected in the pilot contract before legal signs off: 

- A 3-month pilot with a 30-day opt-out that includes a prorated credit for unused committed capacity if we terminate early.
- A ramp schedule that starts at 20% committed capacity month 1, 50% month 2, and 100% by month 3; if we downscale after month 3, we expect a downsell protection credit for the remaining committed months.
- A mutual early termination right with 60 days' notice for either party; if Redwood terminates for convenience, we expect a transition credit equal to one month of committed fees.

I've attached a high-level deal summary and the contract redline we've started on our side. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept opt-out language and the downsell protection? If not, can you escalate to whoever signs off on non-standard termination/ramp terms?

Attachments: Nimble_Deal_Summary_v3.pdf; Nimble_Contract_Redline_20260510.docx

Best,
Claire Barnes
Head of Partnerships, Nimble Health
claire@nimblehealth.com
message_2_subject: Re: Proposal: Pilot + ramp schedule — Nimble Health
message_2_body:
Looping you both in — Nimble wants to add an opt-out and downsell protection to the pilot. Their asks are reasonable commercially, but both the prorated opt-out credit and the downsell protection are non-standard.

My read:
- Opt-out after 30 days would materially increase churn risk. We should offer a 90-day minimum for any credit schedule or cap the credit to 50% of remaining committed fees.
- Ramp schedule is fine; suggest we codify a minimum usage floor (20% of committed) to trigger the ramp protections.
- For Redwood-initiated termination, we should not automatically owe a month of committed fees. Recommend transition support (2 weeks of SRE support) + a one-time credit equal to 25% of one month's committed fees as a compromise.

I attached a redline with my changes. If we need to accept anything outside those guardrails, we should escalate for exec approval: Vivek (GTM) sign-off for price/credit exceptions and CFO-level or Head of Revenue sign-off for any longer-term liability.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Re: Proposal: Pilot + ramp schedule — Nimble Health (escalate to Vivek)
message_3_body:
Agree with Hannah's guardrails. Nimble is a strategic target in healthcare so there's value in flexibility, but we must limit financial exposure. Proposed escalation ask: 

- Approve one-time early termination credit up to 50% of one month's committed fees (cap $20k) if Nimble exercises 30-day opt-out in months 1-3.
- Approve downsell protection: prorated credit for the difference between committed and actual usage for up to 2 billing cycles, capped at 25% of remaining committed value.
- No automatic Redwood-side termination fee; instead offer 2 weeks transition support.
- Any discount to list price or increase to credit cap requires Vivek's approval.

Please escalate to Vivek with the redline and HubSpot deal link. Also flag this as time-sensitive — procurement said they want terms finalized by Friday 2026-05-14 so they can loop Legal.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
message_4_subject: Fwd: Escalation: Nimble pilot — request for opt-out/downsell credit approval (urgent)
message_4_body:
Vivek — forwarding for decision. Quick summary (see thread below and attached redline):

- Customer requests 30-day opt-out with prorated credit for unused committed capacity (months 1-3).
- They want downsell protection after ramp to 100% (prorated credit if they reduce usage).
- Procurement expects finalized language by 2026-05-14.

Recommended ask for your sign-off: authorize up to $20k one-time early-termination credit for a 30-day opt-out window during months 1-3, and allow the 25% cap on downsell credits for up to 2 billing cycles. Any increase beyond those caps requires CFO involvement.
